title: POC weekly sync - onboarding / env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot results, confirm access and infra readiness, and align on next steps for dedicated pilot. Covered docker image access, VPC peering, initial latency QPS numbers, and tuning suggestions (batching/kv cache). Action items include sending security docs and running a 1-hour benchmark with 10k tokens per minute profile.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 & network design doc (Alex) by 2026-03-20
Customer to provide test credentials for staging VPC peering (Lena) by 2026-03-22
Run 1-hour benchmark with 3 model variants and share results (Priya) by 2026-03-24

Lena: Provide VPC peering details and staging IAM account (due 2026-03-22)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Keller (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (NovaHealth Eng Mgr), Maya Lin (NovaHealth ML Lead), Jordan Reyes (NovaHealth Security), Lena Ortiz (NovaHealth DevOps)

Summary: quick check-in on pilot onboarding, confirm network access, review early results and tuning items, list of next steps and owners.

[00:00] Alex (AE): All right folks, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Alex from Redwood, Priya and Tom here too. How's everyone on the customer side?
[00:06] Samir (NovaHealth): Hey Alex, yeah Samir here. Maya, Jordan, Lena with me. Thanks.
[00:10] Maya (NovaHealth): Hi all.
[00:12] Priya (SE): Cool, great. Agenda — run through access status, quick review of the pilot results we uploaded (pilot-run-results.csv), then tuning recs and next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Jordan (Security): Yep - want to call out we still need the SOC2 docs and network diagram to share with our compliance team.
[00:24] Alex (AE): Absolutely, we'll drop the SOC2 link and the network design doc after the call. I'll thumb that into the drive: https://redwood.ai/pilot-security-pack (note: placeholder link).
[00:32] Lena (DevOps): We tried the staging image you provided but hit an auth error when pulling from your container registry. Error message said 401 - unauthorized.
[00:38] Priya (SE): OK, that's on the list. Two likely causes: registry token scope or the IAM role for the node. Samir, can you confirm whether the nodes use an instance profile or static creds for the staging env?
[00:46] Samir: It's instance profile, but it's a cross-account role that we just set up - maybe the trust relationship wasn't fully applied.
[00:52] Priya: Cool. We'll send a short checklist for the cross-account role. Also, you can try the temporary token flow we documented in runbook.md — I'll paste later.
[01:00] Maya: Quick question on the VPC peering: do we need full access to subnets or just to the private endpoint?
[01:06] Alex: For the pilot, private endpoint plus a couple of outbound routes is enough. If you want dedicated capacity later we'll need a broader peering to support autoscaling, but for now keep it minimal.
[01:14] Jordan: Also curious about KMS setup — is key material held by Redwood or customer-managed? We need KMS/HSM control for PHI.
[01:20] Tom (CSM): Great question. We support customer-managed keys via your cloud KMS. For on-prem or air-gapped, we have an HSM integration option too. We'll include the KMS integration doc in the pack.
[01:30] Priya: Switching to results — we ran three variants: open-16b-quant, rwd-13b (float32), and rwd-8b-quant. The CSV has p95 latency and token cost per 1k tokens. Quick highlights: rwd-13b avg p95 was 420ms on the 8-token prefix profile, rwd-8b-quant was ~240ms but higher hallucination rate on a small eval set, and open-16b-quant gave similar latency to 13b but cost was higher.
[01:52] Maya: Do you have the exact numbers for the medical NER prompt set? We care about hallucination risk on diagnosis-related prompts.
[02:00] Priya: Yes - in the pilot-run-results.csv row labeled "med-ner-v2": rwd-13b p95=430ms, accuracy-ish 0.88 (note transcribed as approx), rwd-8b-quant p95=260ms accuracy 0.82, open-16b-quant p95=450ms accuracy 0.87. Those are small-sample results but directional.
[02:20] Samir: Latency numbers look decent. Our SLO for the feature is 500ms p95 so rwd-13b is within that. Cost is still a concern; can you show cost per 1M tokens?
[02:28] Priya: Sure - rough units from the CSV: rwd-13b $120 per 1M tokens, rwd-8b-quant $65 per 1M, open-16b-quant $175 per 1M. Those include GPU amortized plus Redwood runtime. We can tighten quantization or batching to lower it.
[02:44] Lena: On batching, we saw some queueing spike when concurrent QPS went above 120 — is there an autoscaling knob?
[02:50] Priya: Yes, autoscale is driven by concurrency and queue latency thresholds. For the dedicated pilot we can set a max-batch-size and queue-timeout to limit tail latency. Also recommend enabling prefix KV cache for common prompts which reduces per-token work.
[03:06] Maya: How invasive is enabling KV cache? Any data residency concerns?
[03:10] Alex: KV cache caches the model key-value states for prefixes — it's ephemeral and stored on your instance. It doesn't persist to S3 by default. We can enable it within the VPC and it honors your network/KMS controls. Jordan, for PHI this should be acceptable but we'll document the encryption in transit and at rest.
[03:26] Jordan: Good. Please include the encryption at rest details. And where are logs shipped — do you store transcript logs in Redwood or do we push to our SIEM?
[03:34] Tom: We can forward logs to your endpoint (Splunk/Datadog/SIEM). For hosted runs we retain audit logs per the agreed retention; for Private/Dedicated you control retention. We'll send the log pipeline diagram.
[03:46] Samir: About access — what's left for us to do to get peering and the staging run working?
[03:50] Priya: Short list: (1) confirm cross-account role trust (Lena), (2) provide subnet/CIDR for peering (Lena), (3) whitelist the Redwood control-plane egress IPs in your firewall (we'll include the IP list), (4) grant read pull access to the container registry for the staging role.
[04:06] Lena: We can do 1 and 2 by Monday. The firewall whitelisting needs a ticket but can be done.
[04:10] Alex: Perfect. On the tuning front, we recommend three concrete steps: enable KV cache, set max-batch-size to 24 for low tail, and test 4-bit quant variant we can provide — that may hit cost targets while keeping accuracy.
[04:22] Maya: Could you send the eval protocol we should use for hallucination checks? We want consistent scoring across runs.
[04:26] Priya: Yes — eval-protocol.md is in the drive; it includes the prompt set, rubric, and an automated scoring script. We'll share the link.
[04:34] Samir: We want to run a 1-hour stress benchmark that mimics our production distribution — 60% short prompts, 20% 50-token summaries, 20% long context 512-token prompts. Are you able to run that from your side or do we run it from ours?
[04:46] Priya: We can coordinate. For network realism it's better you run from your staging VPC so we measure true peering latency. We'll provide the load script and runner config. We'll also run a mirrored load to compare.
[04:58] Alex: I'll add the load script to the shared folder: pilot-load-scripts.tar.gz. Priya will lead the benchmark.
[05:04] Jordan: Security - one more ask: we need proof of SOC2 Type II and a pen-test summary for the infra.
[05:10] Alex: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and a high-level pen-test summary. For full reports we can do an NDA if needed.
[05:18] Maya: On the model side, curious about fallbacks. If the dedicated pool is saturated do you have automatic fallback to hosted models? We want continuity.
[05:26] Priya: Yes, routing policies can define fallback to cloud-hosted variants with throttling controls. We can set cost-aware fallback to a smaller quant model to keep latency bounds while reducing cost.
[05:36] Samir: Great. That addresses reliability questions.
[05:38] Tom: Quick note on billing: during pilot we'll provide estimated burn rates and a separate pilot invoice — we'll not auto-convert to Reserved until we agree.
[05:46] Alex: OK, time to recap and confirm owners. I'll read back the next steps. First, Redwood: send SOC2, network diagram, KMS and log pipelines, load scripts, and the benchmarking runner config (Alex/Priya) by 2026-03-20.
[05:58] Alex: Customer: provide VPC subnet CIDRs, cross-account IAM role details, and staging credentials (Lena) by 2026-03-22. Maya to share eval prompt set by 2026-03-23. Priya will run the 1-hour benchmark and post CSV results by 2026-03-24.
[06:14] Samir: Sounds good. One more minor item — can you include a cost sensitivity spreadsheet? We want to model 10k, 50k, 200k tokens/day.
[06:22] Alex: Yes we'll attach a cost model spreadsheet - pilot-costs.xlsx.
[06:26] Jordan: Also please include the audit log schema so our SIEM can parse it.
[06:30] Tom: Will do.
[06:32] Maya: Any blockers on our side? We have to clear the firewall ticket but otherwise timeline looks feasible.
[06:36] Lena: We'll triage the firewall ticket today.
[06:38] Alex: Great. Anything else from anyone?
[06:40] Samir: Nope, thank you.
[06:42] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and update the shared folder. Next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc to review benchmark outputs.
[06:50] Maya: Works for us.
[06:52] Alex: Meeting closed.

References and artifacts mentioned: pilot-run-results.csv, pilot-load-scripts.tar.gz, pilot-security-pack (SOC2 & network diagram), eval-protocol.md, pilot-costs.xlsx. Links will be posted to the shared drive after call.

End of transcript.
file_notes: Transcript is verbatim-style with occasional transcription artifacts (numbers transcribed as words, approximate accuracy notes). Speaker labels include roles. Meeting ends with clear next steps and targets for SOC2/docs and benchmarks.
